channel.title: Inspiration Grid — Photography
channel.description: Recent photography inspiration selected by Inspiration Grid.

item.title: Effervescence: Surreal Technicolor Photography by Adewale Mayowa
item.description: Lagos-based photographer and multidisciplinary artist Adewale Mayowa invites us into a bizarre, dreamlike universe with Effervescence, a striking photographic series that explores the boundaries between reality, imagination and the subconscious.

item.title: A Beautiful Kind of Strange: Portraits by Elisa Belitskaya
item.description: Georgian photographer and art director Elisa Belitskaya produces captivating images that combine surreal concepts, theatrical styling and imaginative storytelling.

item.title: Sculptural Fashion & Beauty Photography by Kamilla Hanapova
item.description: Moscow-based Russian photographer and art director Kamilla Hanapova produces fashion, beauty and fine art images that treat clothing as structure and the studio as a stage for imaginary worlds.

item.title: Striking Architectural Photography by Seth Powers
item.description: Shanghai-based photographer Seth Powers specializes in architecture and interiors, capturing contemporary buildings with a keen eye for composition, geometry and light.

item.title: Hilarious, Perfectly Timed Finalists from the 2026 Nikon Comedy Wildlife Awards
item.description: The finalists for the 2026 Nikon Comedy Wildlife Awards have been revealed, offering another entertaining glimpse into the wonderfully unpredictable world of wildlife.

item.title: Bodega Cats of New York: Portraits of the City’s Hardest-Working Felines
item.description: New York writer Dan Rimada and photographer Gulce Kilkis are celebrating one of the city’s most beloved fixtures in Bodega Cats of New York, a new book documenting the feline residents of neighborhood stores across all five boroughs.

item.title: Where Light Falls: Landscape Photography by Martin Rak
item.description: Prague-based photographer Martin Rak returns to the grid with a new selection of images exploring the shifting moods of the natural world.

item.title: Ndebele Superhero: The Vibrant Art of Zana Masombuka
item.description: South African artist Zana Masombuka, also known as Ndebele Superhero, stages striking portraits that carry her heritage and visual culture into the present.

item.title: Timeless Lines: Sam Chick Captures the Beauty of a 1960 Mercedes-Benz 300SL
item.description: UK-based photographer Sam Chick is back on the grid with another beautifully shot automotive series, this time turning his lens toward a rare 1960 Mercedes-Benz 300SL Roadster for classic car specialist Hilton & Moss.

item.title: Through a Painter’s Lens: Portraits by Andrey Yakovlev & Lili Aleeva
item.description: We’ve featured the work of photographer Andrey Yakovlev and art director Lili Aleeva a few times before, and one of the duo’s greatest strengths is their ability to make photography feel remarkably close to painting.

item.title: Where Oil Becomes Landscape: Aerial Images by Kevin Krautgartner
item.description: Kevin Krautgartner is no stranger to Inspiration Grid, and his latest series, Where Oil Becomes Landscape, gives us a bird’s-eye view of Alberta’s oil sands, where resource extraction has transformed huge stretches of land into an industrial terrain of pits, ponds, roads and machinery.

item.title: Feathered Personalities: Bird Photos by Marc Thevissen
item.description: German photographer Marc Thevissen, better known online as Amselon_Pictures, has a passion for capturing the character of birds in the wild.

item.title: Photographer Serhii Fett Erases the Face to Sharpen the Idea
item.description: Serhii Fett is a Ukrainian visual artist and photographer who combines carefully staged photos with a dash of Photoshop magic (and no AI) to produce surreal visual illusions.

item.title: Your Work Deserves a Bigger Stage: A’ Design Award & Competition Call for Submissions
item.description: Think your work belongs among the world’s best? Enter the A’ Design Award and put your work on the international stage.

item.title: Autopilot: Cars as Cultural Objects by Sami Parkkinen
item.description: Autopilot, an ongoing series created by Finnish photographer Sami Parkkinen in collaboration with doctoral researcher Frans Autio, treats cars not as design objects but as evidence, layered with the residue of manufacturing, weather, use and decay.

item.title: The Whale Museum: A New Landmark on Norway’s Arctic Coast
item.description: On the northern coast of Norway, where the rocky landscape meets the open Atlantic, a new cultural landmark is slowly emerging from the terrain. Designed by Danish architect Dorte Mandrup, The Whale is being built in Andenes on the island of Andøya, north of the Arctic Circle.

item.title: Between Places: Minimalist Travel Photography by Jacob Howard
item.description: New Zealand-based photographer and art director Jacob Howard approaches travel with a curiosity for the unknown, turning unfamiliar landscapes into carefully composed studies of place.

item.title: Scientific Artist Wenting Zhu Crystallizes the Seasons in Petri Dishes
item.description: Chinese scientific artist Wenting Zhu turns petri dishes into miniature seasonal landscapes in Crystal Garden: Seasons, a vibrant series created through a delicate collaboration between artistic intention and natural formation.

item.title: Interplanetary Travel: Dani Guindo Turns Iceland Into a Mars Basecamp
item.description: Photographer Dani Guindo captures Iceland as an alien world in Interplanetary Travel, a striking series commissioned by outdoor products manufacturer Heimplanet.

item.title: Nighttime Stories: Neon Portraits by Oliver Takac
item.description: Slovak photographer, colorist and cinematographer Oliver Takáč creates atmospheric images that feel like stills pulled from movies we’ve never seen.

item.title: Versailles Dressed in Red and Blue: Stunning Photography by Aishy
item.description: Paris-based photographer Aishy transforms the Château de Versailles into a vivid collision of color in this series titled Versailles Dressed in Red and Blue.

item.title: Poland and Beyond: Landscape Photography by Mikołaj Gospodarek
item.description: Polish photographer and travel writer Mikołaj Gospodarek captures landscapes shaped by dramatic light, changing seasons and a deep curiosity about place.

item.title: Vienna Symphonies: Monochromatic Architecture by Thomas de Franzoni
item.description: Italian photographer Thomas de Franzoni returns to the grid with Vienna Symphonies, a striking black-and-white study of the city’s architecture as musical notation.

item.title: The Extraordinary Framed Landscapes of Marcin Zajac
item.description: Polish landscape photographer Marcin Zajac has a remarkable ability to reveal familiar places from entirely unexpected perspectives.

item.title: Until the Water: Haunting Portraits of Louisiana’s Changing Landscapes by Frank Relle
item.description: For more than six years, Louisiana photographer Frank Relle has explored the state’s bayous, lakes and swamps after dark, creating a collection of images that feels suspended somewhere between documentary photography and a dream.

item.title: Dramatic Global Landscapes: Photos by Max Terwindt
item.description: Dutch photographer Max Terwindt captures the planet at its most dramatic, travelling from frozen polar regions and volcanic landscapes to deserts, tropical forests and flower-covered fields.

item.title: Tiny Worlds and Everyday Adventures by David Gilliver
item.description: Scottish photographer David Gilliver transforms food, household objects and familiar pop-culture references into playful miniature worlds through his ongoing Little People series.

item.title: Personal Perspectives: A Curated Show Marking 50 Years of Leica Galleries
item.description: Leica Gallery Wetzlar is marking a major milestone with Personal Perspectives, a special exhibition celebrating 50 years of Leica Galleries through 50 photographs selected from across the brand’s international gallery program.

item.title: Spacetime Light Sculptures by Elliot McGucken
item.description: American fine art photographer and physicist Dr. Elliot McGucken turns remote landscapes into stages for luminous cosmic events, suspending spiraling forms of light above deserts, rock formations, coastlines and mountain ranges.

item.title: Cinematic Car Photography by Sevian Daupi
item.description: Modena-based photographer Sevian Daupi captures cars with the eye of a filmmaker, turning automotive shoots into moody scenes filled with atmosphere, movement and style.
